featured_reviews.review_text:
I was down for a day trip to Mumbai and chanced upon Oceanic at Chembur. A Mangalorean restaurant, so its very difficult to go wrong!

I live at Pune and avoid seafood there. But Mumbai is home to the freshest and the best - and so I ordered Prawn Gassi and Neer Dosa and a chilled Fresh Lime Soda..

Prior to settling for this, I had asked the server if I should also order a starter. He advised me against as what I was ordering was enough. Mighty honest of him!

Well, the Prawn Gassi was simply divine. And when combined with Neer Dosa it took the entire combo to a fantastically heavenly level..

The quantity was outstanding and I had to order another round of Neer Dosas and yet another Fresh Lime Soda to polish off the Prawn Gassi!

The decor was simple and the restaurant was super clean 👌
Mood was super and chilled by the AC!
Staff were courteous and helpful...

I hardly visit Mumbai nowadays, but next trip I will again choose to come here to try out newer dishes from their mouth-watering menu.

Rs. 1050/- was bill. And that was very well spent amount 😀

Extremely Disappointed with the Food Quality

I’m genuinely shocked by today’s experience at Malhaar Restaurant.

I had ordered from Zomato , the Veg Kofta was utterly bizarre and it had tutti frutti and cherries in it! Who puts dessert ingredients in a savoury kofta? It felt to me like the chef got confused between making a sweet dish and a main course. I paid ~₹450 for what tasted like a bland, uninspired dessert -definitely not a proper kofta!

The Hyderabadi Chicken too was devoid of flavour, lacking any authentic taste or spice balance. Overall, both dishes were pathetic and not worth the money.

What’s even more disappointing is that this isn’t the first time the quality has dropped. During our previous visit last month, the Manchow Soup we ordered was also far below expectations : watery, poorly seasoned, and lacking the usual flavour punch we associate with Malhaar. The soup wasn't simmered properly.

We’ve been regular customers and always appreciated the food before, but after today’s experience, I’m seriously skeptical about ever ordering from Malhaar again.

featured_reviews.name: Yashank Suvarna
featured_reviews.review_text:
Visited this place yesterday and really enjoyed the overall experience. If you’re someone who loves authentic Maharashtrian cuisine, especially seafood, this place is definitely worth trying. The food quality was genuinely very good and the flavors felt authentic and fresh.

What stood out the most for me was the ambience, the friendliness of the staff, and the overall service. The staff was polite, welcoming, and attentive throughout the visit.

That said, there are a few areas where the restaurant can improve. Firstly, they should consider replacing the plastic glasses with real glass ones, as the current ones had turned yellow over time. Also, the glass served with my cold drink had a noticeable essence/smell of solkadhi, which made the drink feel slightly oily or buttery in taste, I preferred drinking directly through the bottle.

Another thing was the waiting time for the Komdi Vade. The restaurant wasn’t particularly crowded when I visited, but the dish still took around 40 minutes. When I followed up on the order, the waiter went into the kitchen and brought it out within a minute. Since the vade were hot, I’m not sure whether the food had been waiting in the kitchen already or if it was simply a coincidence that it got ready right after I asked.

Overall, despite a few shortcomings, the food and hospitality made the visit enjoyable. A solid 4-star experience.

⭐ 1/5 — Absolutely Disappointing Experience | Would Never Recommend

I visited this place expecting authentic Maratha coastal flavours, but the experience was nothing short of shocking. I ordered a Surmai Tawa Fry, and to my surprise, it was completely tasteless — no spice, no salt, no flavour, nothing. It felt like eating a plain, dry piece of fish.

“We can’t take it back.”

“You have to take it away.”

“We will still charge you for it.”

“We can’t offer you anything else.”

This kind of behaviour is unacceptable for any restaurant claiming to serve good food. Charging a customer for something they didn’t eat and refusing to replace a tasteless dish shows zero professionalism and zero respect.

If the owner doesn’t know how to speak to customers or handle feedback, they are in the wrong business. Food quality below average and service attitude even worse.

Highly NOT recommended.

Coastal Fusion in Chembur is one of those rare restaurants where everything — from the food to the ambience — just falls into place.

I visited recently and started with their Fish Thali, which came loaded with Bangda, Mandeli, Bombil, and Surmai. The flavors were genuinely homestyle and the freshness of the fish was evident in every bite. After that, the Dhaba Style Chicken brought that earthy, slow-cooked richness that you don't find easily anymore. The Kala Masala Chicken Starter stole the show for me — well-spiced, deeply flavored, and gone before I knew it. There's also a Maharashtrian Veg Platter for vegetarians that doesn't feel like an afterthought.

Dessert was Aamras and Gajar Halwa — both done well, a satisfying end to a great meal.

The restaurant is spacious and comfortable, making it a great choice for families and groups. The service was warm and the whole experience felt very genuine.

Highly recommended for anyone craving authentic Maharashtrian and coastal flavors in Chembur.

featured_reviews.review_text:
I visited this place for dinner on Valentine's Day, expecting a lively sports bar with a great crowd and energetic music—similar to what I had seen on their Instagram videos. However, my experience was far from what was portrayed.

Upon arrival, I was informed that the family section was on the second floor, requiring us to climb steep steps. The first floor housed the bar area, where a group of visibly drunk individuals were loudly using foul language. To reach the family section, one has to pass through this bar, which, in appearance and ambiance, felt more like a local dive bar.

When we reached the second floor, the so-called family section, I was immediately disappointed. The space was extremely dark and had a shady atmosphere. Apart from us, only one other couple arrived, but they chose to leave almost instantly. I also wanted to leave, but out of courtesy, I decided to stay and dine since we had already entered.

The setting was uninviting—dimly lit, poorly maintained, and eerily empty on Valentine's Day, a time when most restaurants are bustling. The place was dirty, the menu card was covered in dust, and the food was far below average. Additionally, the seating was uncomfortably low compared to the height of the table, making dining awkward.

To make matters worse, the noise from the bar downstairs was so loud that it disrupted the so-called "family" dining experience. The Instagram videos showcase a vibrant and happening place, but in reality, it was a complete letdown.

This has been, by far, the most disappointing dining experience I've ever had. I would not recommend this place for families or couples—it is more of a beer bar than a proper restaurant.

featured_reviews.review_text: Chembur has my heart & I personally loved this place because of the spacious seating they offer. They have huge outdoor and indoor area and is a perfect place for groups to chill and hangout together. They serve a variety of dishes and I must say their quality and quantity both will surprise you. We tried both their veg and non veg options and were fully content. featured_reviews.name: Adarsh Rajeshirke
featured_reviews.review_text:
Guys, it’s honestly a waste… the place is not worth it at all. The service is extremely slow — you have to wait at least 30 minutes for your order. The staff isn’t trained properly, and they didn’t even seem ready to serve. I saw only 3 people working there.

We ordered bamboo rice, and it was basically just fried rice with a bad omelette and fried noodles — didn’t make any sense. After waiting around 40 minutes, they came and said there were no eggs for the omelette.

The starters were tasteless — everything had the same flavor, mostly like tomato ketchup. Due to gas shortage, they’ve reduced their menu to about 40%, and no Indian dishes are available. When we tried ordering the main course, they were pushing us to order pizza and pasta instead.

The ambience is good, but what’s the point if the food isn’t worth the price? Don’t go by the hype — it’s genuinely a waste of money.

featured_reviews.name: Umair Lucky
featured_reviews.review_text:
If you are looking for a place where quality meets quantity in the most elegant way possible, Global Fusion is the ultimate destination. I recently visited for a weekend dinner, and honestly, I am still thinking about the experience. It isn’t just a meal; it’s an absolute marathon of flavors.
The Ambience and Vibe
From the moment you walk in, the atmosphere sets the tone. The decor is sophisticated, featuring beautiful water bodies, ambient lighting, and a spacious layout that makes it feel premium despite being a popular, busy spot. It’s perfect for everything from a romantic date night to a loud, celebratory family dinner.
The Food: A Deep Dive
The star of the show here is undoubtedly the buffet, which leans heavily toward Asian and Seafood specialties. Unlike many buffets where food sits out getting cold, Global Fusion serves a significant portion of their appetizers right to your table, piping hot.
The Sushi & Sashimi: The sushi conveyor belt (or the platter service) is a dream. The fish was incredibly fresh, and the variety of vegetarian and non-vegetarian rolls was impressive.
Starters: This is where they truly shine. The Prawns Tempura were crispy and light, and the Chicken Teriyaki had the perfect glaze. If you enjoy dim sum, their baskets are translucent, delicate, and packed with flavor.
Main Course: By the time you get to the mains, you might be struggling, but don’t skip the Burmese Khow Suey or their signature fish in black bean sauce. The flavors are authentic and not "dumbed down."
Desserts: Save room! From the Baskin Robbins ice cream station to the chocolate fountain and the tiny, elegant pastries, the dessert spread is a grand finale in every sense.
Service & Hospitality
The staff deserves a special shout-out. Despite the restaurant being at full capacity, the service was seamless. Our servers were attentive, clearing plates quickly and ensuring the "unlimited" starters kept flowing without us having to ask twice.
The Verdict
Is it pricey? Yes, it’s a bit of an investment. But considering the premium seafood, the sheer variety of cuisines (Japanese, Chinese, Indian, and more), and the high-end service, it is worth every penny.

featured_reviews.name: Sachchin Annam
featured_reviews.review_text:
Global Fusion is a well-known dining spot in Chembur, offering an impressive spread of global cuisines with a strong highlight on seafood variety.

The restaurant stands out for its extensive selection of fresh and flavorful seafood dishes,ranging from Asian-style preparations to continental favorites and making it a great choice for seafood lovers looking to explore different tastes in one place.

One of the key strengths of Global Fusion is its attentive and accommodating staff. They are always willing to help customize orders based on preferences, whether it’s adjusting spice levels, suggesting combinations, or catering to specific dietary needs.

Additionally, the service is quick and efficient, ensuring a smooth dining experience even during busy hours. The combination of diverse food options, flexibility in service, and prompt attention makes it a reliable choice for both casual dining and special outings.

featured_reviews.name: Ishrat Shaikh
featured_reviews.review_text:
We had an amazing family dinner at Global Fusion, Chembur, and it was truly one of the best dining experiences we've had. The food was absolutely delicious, especially their sushi, which was fresh, authentic, and one of the best we've tasted.

If you're a dumpling lover, this place is a must-visit! The variety and quality of the dumplings were exceptional. We were also impressed by the freshness and quality of the prawns and fish, which were perfectly prepared and full of flavor.
The staff was incredibly friendly and attentive throughout our visit. A special thanks to Kiran, who looked after us from start to finish and ensured we had a wonderful experience. Her warm hospitality and excellent service made our evening even more memorable.

Global Fusion is the perfect destination for a family dinner, offering amazing food, outstanding service, and a great ambiance. Whether you're craving sushi, dumplings, seafood, or authentic Asian cuisine, this is a place you should not miss. Highly recommended

featured_reviews.name: Reehan Gazge
featured_reviews.review_text: Global Fusion in Chembur offers a lively buffet experience with elegant interiors and a festive atmosphere, perfect for groups and celebrations. The highlight is the extensive starter selection — sushi, tempura, kebabs, and seafood are fresh and flavorful, often overshadowing the mains. While the main course is diverse, some dishes feel safe and lack boldness. Desserts are plentiful but uneven; chocolate mousse impresses, while some Indian sweets are dry. Service is warm and attentive, though slightly slower during peak hours. Overall, it’s a vibrant, value-for-money buffet with excellent starters and ambience, despite minor flaws in mains and desserts.

featured_reviews.name: Faiz F
featured_reviews.review_text:
​Global Fusion in Chembur truly lives up to its reputation as a premier destination for a buffet dinner. The restaurant excels in providing a diverse and high-quality dining experience, making it a fantastic choice for anyone looking for great variety, especially in the initial courses.

​The sheer choice of multiple starters in both vegetarian and non-vegetarian selections is arguably the highlight, ensuring every palate finds something exciting. We especially found the sushi and salads highly recommended—they were fresh, flavorful, and presented beautifully, providing a delightful start to the meal.

​While the selection in the main course was limited, which is perhaps the only area for improvement, the dining experience finished on a high note. The desserts and ice creams have good options and taste great, offering a satisfying and sweet conclusion to the feast.

​A special mention must go to Mr. Shetty, the Manager, whose dedication to service and best-in-class hospitality was evident in the seamless management of the floor. His efforts truly enhanced the overall atmosphere and experience.

​We have a couple of suggestions that could make the experience perfect: using table number clips for starter ordering would streamline the process further, and adding more options in the Mutton starters would cater to a wider range of preferences.

​Overall, Global Fusion Chembur offers incredible value and a memorable night out.
